decisive_items: enlarged testis, epididymis, and infected appendages
purulent foci were visible on the surface of the vessels, and their texture was tough and inseparable
Pus culture isolated P. aeruginosa, susceptible to ceftazidime and ofloxacin
response.rationale: The vignette describes acute infection of both testis and epididymis with purulent foci and P. aeruginosa, matching epididymo-orchitis. Other candidates are either too narrow (orchitis, epididymitis), contradicted (torsion), or represent consequences (hemorrhagic infarction) rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Only testis inflammation, misses epididymis and infection specifics.
Urine analysis negative, no UTI evidence.
Chronic epididymitis contradicts acute 5-day history and purulent foci.
Occult penis is a congenital finding, not the acute scrotal diagnosis.
Hemorrhagic infarction is a pathological consequence, not the primary clinical diagnosis.
Epididymitis alone omits testis involvement and infection details.
Explicitly no torsion evident in sperm vessels, contradicting torsion.
Pyocele implies a pus collection, but only purulent foci on vessels are described.
Infected testicular appendage is too narrow, ignoring epididymis and testis.
